title: Specify owned TX grants and conflict resolution
description:
Scope: assignment/grant encoding in /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/spec/02b-ccp-receiver-aware.md. Define owner identity, applicable intervals, receiver/radio exclusions, validity and bounded assignment counts. Specify how standing grants interact with committed RX and half-duplex resources, and identify the selected assignment or collision-repair semantics. Independent event examples must distinguish a hash candidate from an exclusive opportunity. Reuse project-LICHEN-worker6-b7z9.22 mechanics without treating anonymous slot maps as assignments to every listener.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Keep standing coordination rather than introducing per-packet reservation traffic. Preserve useful sorted/bounded slot validation and replace only the obsolete ownership interpretation.
acceptance_criteria: Exact grant fields and ownership rules are specified. Independent timelines reject sender-grant-only access, overlapping receiver TX/RX, priority TX preempting committed RX, and ambiguous anonymous ownership. Equal modulo-eight hash residues remain colliding across SFN rotation until the specified assignment/repair resolves them. Unassigned fallback remains explicitly contended; no delivery or collision-free guarantee is invented.
